- Integrated manufacturing capabilities and expanded infrastructure following the operationalization and stabilization of Unit-3
- Diversified product portfolio across elevator cabins, automatic doors, traction machines and cabin safety frames
- Growing branch and dealer network, with new branch offices in Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata enhancing customer outreach and service delivery
- Experienced management team and a workforce of 204 permanent employees and workmen as on March 31, 2026
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility (stainless steel, steel, electrical components) — Management states these inputs constitute a significant portion of production costs and that fluctuations in commodity prices may impact profitability if cost increases cannot be passed on to customers. The steel polishing business is separately described as sensitive to stainless steel prices, raw material availability and import regulations.
- Intense competition in a fragmented elevator industry — The elevator industry remains highly competitive with multinational corporations, unorganized domestic players and regional manufacturers competing on price, technology, quality and service — a structural cap on pricing power for a component supplier.
- Cyclicality — economic slowdown in construction and real estate — Any slowdown in construction activity, real estate investments, industrial growth or infrastructure spending may adversely affect demand for elevator products; the Company's demand is entirely derived from the building cycle.
- Supply chain and operational disruption — Exposure to supply chain disruptions, logistics challenges, geopolitical developments, transportation constraints and freight cost fluctuations, which may affect procurement schedules, production planning, inventory management and timely deliveries to customers.
- Technology and innovation obsolescence — Rapid technological advancement and evolving customer expectations require continuous investment in product development, manufacturing processes, automation and quality enhancement; failure to adapt may impair competitive position and long-term growth prospects.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Changes in taxation policies, environmental regulations, labour laws, safety standards and other statutory requirements may increase compliance obligations and operational costs — material for a business whose product access depends on safety and fire-rating standards.
- Financial risk — interest rates, forex, receivables and working capital — Management flags exposure to interest rate and foreign exchange fluctuations, credit risk on customer receivables and working capital management challenges; the year's profit decline was itself attributed partly to higher finance costs following capacity expansion.
- Human resource / skilled manpower availability — Continued growth depends on attracting, developing and retaining skilled personnel; increasing competition for talent and availability of trained manpower may constrain operations and future expansion plans.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Aaron Industries operates in two primary business segments. The Elevator Division manufactures and supplies elevator cabins, automatic door systems, traction machines, cabin safety frames and various elevator components to elevator OEMs and installers, and during the year obtained fire door certification enabling entry into specialised installations such as hospitals and fire-compliant buildings. The Steel Polishing Division undertakes polishing, finishing and processing of stainless-steel sheets both for the Company's own elevator products and for third-party customers, supporting its backward integration strategy by improving quality control and reducing dependence on external processors.

outlook.body:
- Enhance capacity utilization of existing manufacturing facilities including Unit-3 — now operationalized and stabilized — to achieve economies of scale and improve productivity
- Strengthen market presence by expanding the footprint across India through the branch network and dealer relationships, including new branch offices in Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata
- Grow the elevator products business by increasing market share in elevator cabins, automatic door systems, cabin safety frames and other elevator components
- Expand the export business by exploring new international markets and strengthening existing export relationships to diversify revenue streams
- Operational excellence and cost optimization across manufacturing efficiency, supply chain management, inventory controls and resource utilization
- Technology and product innovation — product development, automation and safety-enhanced, technologically advanced elevator products
- Leverage backward integration through the stainless-steel polishing division for quality control, supply chain reliability, cost efficiencies and value addition
- Strengthen the financial position through disciplined working capital management, cash flow optimization and prudent financial management
- Focus on quality and compliance — leveraging certifications, including fire-rated elevator door certifications, to address high-specification projects across residential, commercial, industrial, healthcare and infrastructure sectors
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's principal expansion of the year was Unit-3: management states it has "successfully operationalized and stabilized Unit-3" and is now focused on maximizing capacity utilization, improving operational efficiencies and strengthening market presence across key geographies. No location, size or rupee quantum for Unit-3 is disclosed in the routed text. Management explicitly attributes the year's profitability decline to "higher depreciation, finance costs, and other expenses associated with capacity expansion and business growth initiatives undertaken by the Company", confirming the expansion was funded and capitalised during FY2025-26. Distribution-side expansion consists of new branch offices in Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata, intended to enhance customer outreach and service delivery, alongside expansion of the dealer network across India. The stainless-steel polishing division continues as the backward-integration leg, processing sheets for internal elevator production as well as third-party customers. Forward capex intent is stated only qualitatively — continuing investment in technology, process improvements, product development and automation — with no announced project, timeline or amount.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Outlook remains positive, supported by continued growth of the Indian elevator industry, increasing urbanization, infrastructure development and rising demand for quality elevator products and components
- Demand for elevators driven by growth in housing, commercial complexes, hospitals, hotels, educational institutions, metro projects, airports and industrial facilities
- Rapid urban migration and scarcity of urban land encouraging vertical development, increasing elevator installations in residential and commercial projects
- A large installed base of aging elevators across India presents significant opportunity for modernization, replacement and upgradation
- Growing regulatory focus on fire safety standards is increasing demand for certified elevator products; the Company's fire door certification strengthens its competitive position in that segment
- Increasing acceptance of Indian-manufactured engineering products in international markets presents export growth opportunities
- Backward integration via the stainless-steel polishing division provides quality assurance, supply chain control, reduced lead times and improved cost efficiencies
- Indian elevator market remains highly fragmented — multinationals, organized domestic manufacturers and regional players — where product quality, customization, delivery timelines and after-sales support are the differentiators
- Stainless-steel processing/polishing demand growing from construction, architecture, elevators, hospitality, transportation, healthcare and industrial sectors, with customers preferring premium finishes and value-added products
- Margin narrative: EBITDA margin improved to 19.22% during the year from 19.01% in the previous year, reflecting improved operational efficiencies, cost optimization and the benefits of integrated manufacturing operations, while profitability declined primarily due to higher depreciation, finance costs and other expenses associated with capacity expansion
- Steel polishing / elevator input costs remain sensitive to stainless steel price fluctuations, raw material availability and import regulations

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aaron Industries Limited manufactures elevator cabins, automatic door systems, traction machines and elevator components for India's fragmented elevator value chain, backed by an in-house stainless-steel polishing division that gives it backward integration.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Aaron Industries operates in two primary business segments. The Elevator Division manufactures and supplies elevator cabins, automatic door systems, traction machines, cabin safety frames and various elevator components to elevator OEMs and installers, and during the year obtained fire door certification enabling entry into specialised installations such as hospitals and fire-compliant buildings. The Steel Polishing Division undertakes polishing, finishing and processing of stainless-steel sheets both for the Company's own elevator products and for third-party customers, supporting its backward integration strategy by improving quality control and reducing dependence on external processors.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Outlook remains positive, supported by continued growth of the Indian elevator industry, increasing urbanization, infrastructure development and rising demand for quality elevator products and components
- Demand for elevators driven by growth in housing, commercial complexes, hospitals, hotels, educational institutions, metro projects, airports and industrial facilities
- Rapid urban migration and scarcity of urban land encouraging vertical development, increasing elevator installations in residential and commercial projects
- A large installed base of aging elevators across India presents significant opportunity for modernization, replacement and upgradation
- Growing regulatory focus on fire safety standards is increasing demand for certified elevator products; the Company's fire door certification strengthens its competitive position in that segment
- Increasing acceptance of Indian-manufactured engineering products in international markets presents export growth opportunities
- Backward integration via the stainless-steel polishing division provides quality assurance, supply chain control, reduced lead times and improved cost efficiencies
- Indian elevator market remains highly fragmented — multinationals, organized domestic manufacturers and regional players — where product quality, customization, delivery timelines and after-sales support are the differentiators
- Stainless-steel processing/polishing demand growing from construction, architecture, elevators, hospitality, transportation, healthcare and industrial sectors, with customers preferring premium finishes and value-added products
- Margin narrative: EBITDA margin improved to 19.22% during the year from 19.01% in the previous year, reflecting improved operational efficiencies, cost optimization and the benefits of integrated manufacturing operations, while profitability declined primarily due to higher depreciation, finance costs and other expenses associated with capacity expansion
- Steel polishing / elevator input costs remain sensitive to stainless steel price fluctuations, raw material availability and import regulations

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Enhance capacity utilization of existing manufacturing facilities including Unit-3 — now operationalized and stabilized — to achieve economies of scale and improve productivity
- Strengthen market presence by expanding the footprint across India through the branch network and dealer relationships, including new branch offices in Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata
- Grow the elevator products business by increasing market share in elevator cabins, automatic door systems, cabin safety frames and other elevator components
- Expand the export business by exploring new international markets and strengthening existing export relationships to diversify revenue streams
- Operational excellence and cost optimization across manufacturing efficiency, supply chain management, inventory controls and resource utilization
- Technology and product innovation — product development, automation and safety-enhanced, technologically advanced elevator products
- Leverage backward integration through the stainless-steel polishing division for quality control, supply chain reliability, cost efficiencies and value addition
- Strengthen the financial position through disciplined working capital management, cash flow optimization and prudent financial management
- Focus on quality and compliance — leveraging certifications, including fire-rated elevator door certifications, to address high-specification projects across residential, commercial, industrial, healthcare and infrastructure sectors

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's principal expansion of the year was Unit-3: management states it has "successfully operationalized and stabilized Unit-3" and is now focused on maximizing capacity utilization, improving operational efficiencies and strengthening market presence across key geographies. No location, size or rupee quantum for Unit-3 is disclosed in the routed text. Management explicitly attributes the year's profitability decline to "higher depreciation, finance costs, and other expenses associated with capacity expansion and business growth initiatives undertaken by the Company", confirming the expansion was funded and capitalised during FY2025-26. Distribution-side expansion consists of new branch offices in Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata, intended to enhance customer outreach and service delivery, alongside expansion of the dealer network across India. The stainless-steel polishing division continues as the backward-integration leg, processing sheets for internal elevator production as well as third-party customers. Forward capex intent is stated only qualitatively — continuing investment in technology, process improvements, product development and automation — with no announced project, timeline or amount.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Backward integration through the in-house stainless-steel polishing division, providing quality assurance, supply chain control, reduced lead times and improved cost efficiencies
- Fire door certification (IS 17518: Part 2: 2021, ISO 3008-2:2017, EN 81-58:2018) enabling entry into specialised elevator installations including hospitals and fire-compliant buildings
- Integrated manufacturing capabilities and expanded infrastructure following the operationalization and stabilization of Unit-3
- Diversified product portfolio across elevator cabins, automatic doors, traction machines and cabin safety frames
- Growing branch and dealer network, with new branch offices in Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata enhancing customer outreach and service delivery
- Experienced management team and a workforce of 204 permanent employees and workmen as on March 31, 2026

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material price volatility (stainless steel, steel, electrical components) — Management states these inputs constitute a significant portion of production costs and that fluctuations in commodity prices may impact profitability if cost increases cannot be passed on to customers. The steel polishing business is separately described as sensitive to stainless steel prices, raw material availability and import regulations.
- Intense competition in a fragmented elevator industry — The elevator industry remains highly competitive with multinational corporations, unorganized domestic players and regional manufacturers competing on price, technology, quality and service — a structural cap on pricing power for a component supplier.
- Cyclicality — economic slowdown in construction and real estate — Any slowdown in construction activity, real estate investments, industrial growth or infrastructure spending may adversely affect demand for elevator products; the Company's demand is entirely derived from the building cycle.
- Supply chain and operational disruption — Exposure to supply chain disruptions, logistics challenges, geopolitical developments, transportation constraints and freight cost fluctuations, which may affect procurement schedules, production planning, inventory management and timely deliveries to customers.
- Technology and innovation obsolescence — Rapid technological advancement and evolving customer expectations require continuous investment in product development, manufacturing processes, automation and quality enhancement; failure to adapt may impair competitive position and long-term growth prospects.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — Changes in taxation policies, environmental regulations, labour laws, safety standards and other statutory requirements may increase compliance obligations and operational costs — material for a business whose product access depends on safety and fire-rating standards.
- Financial risk — interest rates, forex, receivables and working capital — Management flags exposure to interest rate and foreign exchange fluctuations, credit risk on customer receivables and working capital management challenges; the year's profit decline was itself attributed partly to higher finance costs following capacity expansion.
- Human resource / skilled manpower availability — Continued growth depends on attracting, developing and retaining skilled personnel; increasing competition for talent and availability of trained manpower may constrain operations and future expansion plans.
